offerings.name: De-Sludge
offerings.description: Removes internal friction ('sludge') in processes, culture, capability and technology that stops an organisation from actually being customer-centric.

offerings.name: EAS (Effort Assessment Score)
offerings.description: Measures and reduces customer effort across time, physical, cognitive and emotional dimensions at every touchpoint in a journey.

offerings.name: Experiential Segmentation
offerings.description: Segments customers by the experience they seek (not demographics), so engagement, service and communication can be tailored to what each segment actually values.

offerings.name: JUMP
offerings.description: Behavioural design for digital adoption and engagement — fixes friction in digital/app/web journeys using behavioural-science design principles.

offerings.name: ME (Marketing Effectiveness)
offerings.description: Uses the Friction x Motivation x Context model and behavioural nudges to fix positioning, communication and persistency/retention problems.

case_studies.industry: Consumer Electronics, PCs & Software (global, 160 countries)
case_studies.finding: Shift to a services-led model created internal friction and attrition; CX not seen as a competitive differentiator; disparate systems limited visibility of customer information.
case_studies.outcome: Reduced attrition, servitization shift, enhanced strategic alignment.

case_studies.industry: Steel Manufacturing (B2B, industrial, 500+ customers)
case_studies.finding: Severe commoditization and market-share loss; customers perceive the vendor as transaction-oriented; customer centricity siloed to Sales/Customer Service; no contract-profitability review before signing.
case_studies.outcome: 1.4X wallet-share growth; re-acquired 'preferred supplier' status; 17% increase in profitability.

case_studies.industry: Paints & Speciality Coatings Manufacturing (consumer + B2B)
case_studies.finding: Differing cultural contexts across business units caused disengagement/attrition; low scores on strategic alignment, customer insight and cross-functional collaboration; repetitive, undifferentiated sales cycle.
case_studies.outcome: Complaint redressal time down by half.

case_studies.industry: Pharma / OTC (B2B buying committee)
case_studies.finding: No visibility into a multi-stakeholder buying committee's real decision drivers.

case_studies.industry: Manufacturing — capital equipment / diesel engines, pump sets (B2B dealer & distributor channel)
case_studies.finding: Brand perceived as laid-back, causing erosion; dealers feel undercut by direct-to-customer service; one-size-fits-all treatment of sites; no structured escalation matrix.

case_studies.industry: Banking (5th-largest-in-Asia scale; branch, mobile app & internet banking)
case_studies.finding: High cost of customer service via physical channels; digital touchpoints/app perceived as inconsistent and unreliable; friction and cognitive load peak in the fund-transfer flow (Money Anxiety / Empathy Gap).

case_studies.industry: Life Insurance — Top-4 private player, affluent segment (agency/advisor channel)
case_studies.finding: Lack of market share in the affluent segment; perceived as exclusively sales-focused with weak post-purchase engagement.

case_studies.industry: Life Insurance — premium renewal & persistency (advisor and digital renewal channels)
case_studies.finding: Low persistency after year 3-5; over 63% of customers not aware or comfortable with digital payment gateways for renewals; renewal letters don't explain the product.

case_studies.industry: Agrochemical (channel-based sales org; retailer network, SIO & call-centre channel)
case_studies.finding: Brand positioned as a 'port of last call'; loyalty programme seen as earn & burn; call centre is a high-friction primary touchpoint; withdrawn products not communicated to retailers; no proactive complaint follow-up.

case_studies.industry: Electrical Engineering — distributors, dealers, RURBAN markets
case_studies.finding: Driving Channel Engagement (Electricals) — wallet share kept shrinking despite product-quality improvements; brand couldn't break the market leader's 'halo effect'; automating channel processes drove latent dealer disengagement.

case_studies.industry: Premium & Affluent Private Banking (relationship-manager-led channel)
case_studies.finding: Leading Bank Leverages Experiential Segments (Affluent Program) — high NPS but low referral/recommendation growth; relationship managers not effective in support or service recovery.

case_studies.industry: Personal Loans & Lending (branch and channel-based sales org)
case_studies.finding: Leading Financial Institution Goes Experiential (Personal Loans) — over 37% of bank clients switched provider in 6-12 months; a late-stage interest-rate surprise near the end of the loan journey broke trust (cognitive dissonance -> ego depletion).

case_studies.industry: Capital / Material Handling Equipment (global service network)
case_studies.finding: High commoditization with insignificant switching barriers and low engagement; high MTBF reliability story overshadowed by cost and turnaround-time complaints.

case_studies.industry: Organised Retail — electronics (B2C, 1000+ outlets)
case_studies.finding: B2C Goes Experiential (Electronics Retail) — customers treated homogenously regardless of whether they care most about price, convenience or relationship.

case_studies.industry: Broking / Trading (financial franchise & dealer network)
case_studies.finding: Driving Digital Adoption — active customer base a small percentage of a much larger total base; high-volume clients paying competitors for extras not offered; new investors treated as a hobby segment.

case_studies.industry: Premium Banking (relationship-manager-led channel)
case_studies.finding: Leading Financial Institution Goes Experiential (Premium Banking) — loyalty programme tracking & redemption so high-friction it caused disengagement; one-size-fits-all onboarding addressed only immediate needs.

case_studies.industry: Retail Banking (mobile banking app; branch & contact centre)
case_studies.finding: High cost of customer service via physical channels despite launching a banking app; customers can't find the fund-transfer option and give up (Money Anxiety / Empathy Gap, Peak 1 friction).
case_studies.outcome: Reduction in Cost to Serve / Higher Digital Adoption.

case_studies.industry: General / Motor Insurance (insurer purchase-journey website)
case_studies.finding: Losing market share to online-first competitors; customers abandon the application mid-document-upload due to unclear guidelines and unnecessary iterations.
case_studies.outcome: Increase in market share via digital channel.

case_studies.industry: Industrial B2B — Material Handling Equipment (B2B self-service portal)
case_studies.finding: Sales team stuck on AMC/renewal work rather than new consultative business; sign-up screens have too many fields; field engineers unsure whether an asset is in-warranty or in-AMC.
case_studies.outcome: From Cost Centre to Profit Centre; Wallet-Share and Profitability objectives.

case_studies.industry: Electricals & Consumer Durables (D2C e-commerce + WhatsApp/chatbot)
case_studies.finding: Built an e-commerce site to match Amazon/Flipkart but customers still default to dealers; chatbot/search gives no help and no re-engagement nudge; WhatsApp bot's 11-item list violates Hick's Law.

case_studies.industry: Financial Institution / Personal Lending (branch & DSA channel)
case_studies.finding: More than 37% of bank clients switched provider in 6-12 months; customers expect differential treatment but receive one-size-fits-all service (segmented instead into Speedsters/Needers/Value Speedsters/Value Needers).

case_studies.industry: Private / Priority (Affluent) Banking Programs
case_studies.finding: Leading Bank, Affluent Program — loyal affluent customers rarely refer friends/family despite loyalty; relationship managers not effective in support or service recovery; awareness of programme benefits very low.

case_studies.industry: Life Insurance (agency and digital renewal channels)
case_studies.finding: Driving Growth in Life Insurance — low persistency after year 1/3/5; over 75% of premium still collected through non-digital methods.

case_studies.industry: Life Insurance (contact centre & renewal communication)
case_studies.finding: Driving Persistency in Life Insurance — customers lack understanding of the policy as a product/financial instrument; renewal communications feel disjointed across the lifecycle.

case_studies.industry: Pharma / OTC Consumer Health (probiotic supplements; doctor & pharmacist channel)
case_studies.finding: From Illness to Wellness — product only bought when prescribed alongside antibiotics; pharmacists don't drive recommendation; one undifferentiated message sent to all segments.
case_studies.outcome: Enhanced market share from repositioning and redefined communication.

case_studies.industry: Manufacturing — Capital Equipment / Material Handling (B2B, key accounts)
case_studies.finding: Driving Accelerated Growth — high commoditization stretching the sales cycle; product revenue plateauing while services revenue stays flat; key accounts get one-size-fits-all engagement.

banking_industry_index.note: Banking is a cross-offering industry: a single banking query can legitimately surface case studies from up to 4 different offerings at once.

business_challenge_signals.signal: Friction / high-effort customer or channel touchpoints (umbrella 'sludge' signal)
One-size-fits-all treatment of customers, sites, or key accounts
High / rising cost to serve via physical channels (branches, call centres, RMs)
Commoditization / no real differentiation / low switching barriers
Loyalty or affluent programme not translating into advocacy, referral or genuine behaviour change ('earn & burn')
Weak or stalled digital adoption despite app/digital investment
Digital journey overloaded with steps, fields, or options (Hick's-Law-type friction)
Customer switching / high churn despite retention effort
Policy lapse / low persistency after year 1, 3, 5
Relationship managers / frontline reps not resolving issues or driving deeper engagement
No structured escalation / complaint-resolution process
Dealer/channel-partner conflict or disengagement
Undifferentiated, one-message-fits-all communication across distinct segments
Customers not comfortable with or aware of digital payment methods for renewals/premiums
Lack of understanding of the product/category itself, undermining renewal or trust
Wallet share shrinking or plateauing despite product/service improvements
Small active base within a much larger total customer base
Multi-stakeholder B2B buying committee decision drivers unclear
Brand lacks top-of-mind recall / seen as a 'last resort' in its category
Customer perceives vendor/brand as purely transactional, not a partner
Customer-centricity or CX ownership siloed to one function
Losing market share to online-first / e-commerce competitors

outcome_language.outcome: From cost centre to profit centre / velocity of sales / profitability

EAS: Time / Physical / Cognitive / Emotional effort dimensions
Money Anxiety / Empathy Gap journey mapping
ES: Self Made Tycoon / Steel Grey / PSB Migrant / Mature & Emerging Professionals (banking archetypes)
JUMP: Hick's Law, Chunking, Spark Effect, Loss Aversion, Framing, Priming
ME: FMC Model (Friction x Motivation x Context = Behaviour)
Emotional Anchors (Contextual Relevance, Transparency, Consistency, Flexibility)

eval_questions.query: Digital channels are cheaper to run, but customers still flood our branches for basic banking.
Customers get stuck partway through the mobile-banking transfer flow and just give up.
Our affluent banking customers report high NPS but almost never refer anyone — how do we convert satisfaction into growth?
Our relationship managers aren't resolving complaints well, and it's undermining the premium banking experience.
More than a third of our banking customers switched providers in the last year despite our retention efforts.
Loan applicants tell us the process feels great right up until we surprise them with a different interest rate near the end.
Our contact-centre and branch costs keep climbing even though we launched a banking app.
Our loyalty programme's redemption process is so clunky that customers seem to check out right after they try to claim a reward.
Our affluent banking customers are happy but not engaged — what's really driving that gap?
Our contact-centre and RM network keeps getting more expensive to run even as we push digital.
Our personal-loan customers get the same one-size-fits-all treatment regardless of who they are.
